To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel gene delivery system that can be used for the targeted delivery of the sodium/iodide symporter gene to EGFR expressing tumor cells and that this system is capable of inducing iodine uptake in tumors and can be used for systemic therapy of metastatic liver tumors.

systemic delivery of NIS-expresscing plasmid using polyplexes conjugated with an EGFR-specific ligand is capable to induce tumor-specific uptake of radioiodide, which can be therapeutically exploited for treatment of metastatic cancers.
the novel polyplexes are capable of inducing tumor-selective iodine uptake in hepatocellular carcinoma xenografts and are therapeutically effective in a metastatic model of hepatocellular carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new strategy for the treatment of metastatic cancer.
the development of a novel non-viral polyplex-mediated EGFR-targeted gene therapy approach for liver cancer.
the design of a novel polyplex system for the systemic delivery of a therapeutic gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study show that systemic NIS-gene transfer using polyplex coupled with an EGFr-targeting ligand can induce tumor-specific iodide accumulation, representing a promising strategy of systemic NIS gene radiotherapy for the treatment of metastatic cancer.
the use of the GE11-targeted polyplex is a promising novel approach for systemic NIS-gene therapy in metastatic liver tumors and possibly other EGFR-positive tumors.
the use of polyplexes coupled to an EGFR-specific ligand for systemic NIS delivery is a promising approach to induce tumor-selective iodine uptake and to treat metastatic liver cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of polyplexes coupled to an EGF-specific ligand for NIS gene therapy is a promising innovative strategy to treat metastatic cancer.
the combination of NIS gene delivery with polymeric carriers and EGFR-targeting agents is a promising novel approach for the systemic therapy of EGFR-positive cancers.
NIS gene delivery to tumors using polyplexes conjugated with an EGFR targeting ligand can be an innovative strategy for systemic therapy of metastatic cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a novel gene therapy approach for the treatment of metastatic cancers.
we have shown for the first time the possibility of using polyplexes to deliver the sodium iodide transporter (NIS) to cancer cells.
the NIS gene can be delivered by nonviral gene transfer and targeted to tumors by using a ligand specific for the tumor-associated EGFR, which is overexpressed in many types of cancer.
